evidence: Traupman 260, 304: hōrologium digitāle, a digital clock
terms.comment: The modern sense, from English “digit”, a figure. Classically digitālis means “of a finger”, as in a finger’s thickness (Plin. NH 22.48, Lewis & Short), so the modern sense is a borrowing, not a classical one. Morgan–Owens lists “digital (opp. analog)” without a Latin word.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 260, 304, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. digital (opp. analog).
